rationale: Chris brings CTO-level expertise in robotics simulation at Zhavia Labs, while Miguel is building real-time robotics control software and hardware infrastructure with recent experience at NVIDIA and Cisco. Both are based in San Francisco and work across the robotics stack—Chris on simulation and Miguel on embedded systems and firmware—making them natural collaborators for bridging simulation-to-hardware challenges.
intro_message: Chris Orlin Cardoza, meet Miguel Villa Floran — you're both working on robotics systems from different angles (simulation vs. embedded/firmware), and Miguel's hardware bring-up experience could complement Zhavia's simulation work.
